description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for three different measures—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—across a range of initial confidence values from 0.81 to 0.99. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 0.01, ranging from 0.81 to 0.99. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with major gridlines at 0.2 intervals. The blue line with square markers, representing Final Accuracy, starts at approximately 1.0 when initial confidence is 0.81 and remains consistently high, fluctuating slightly around 0.95 to 1.0, with a slight dip to about 0.92 at an initial confidence of 0.95 before rising again. The green line with circular markers, representing Initial Accuracy, begins at approximately 0.55 and shows a general upward trend, reaching about 0.95 at an initial confidence of 0.99. The orange line with diamond markers, representing Δ Accuracy, starts at approximately 0.45 and exhibits a downward trend, decreasing to about 0.03 at an initial confidence of 0.99. Error bars are present for all data points, indicating variability in the measurements.
